description:
Telegram Channel Scraper: Public Posts, Views & Media

Scrape public Telegram channels via the t.me web preview: one row per post with text, date, views, media, link previews, polls, reactions, hashtags and links, plus channel info. No login, no API key, no browser. $0.30 per 1,000 posts.

Pricing (pay per event, billed to your Apify account): Post: $0.0003; Channel info: $0.001; platform usage billed to your account.

Runs on Apify as subimpact/telegram-channel-scraper.

_maxChargeUsd.description: Per-run spending cap in USD (default 0.5). Passed to Apify as the run option maxTotalChargeUsd, so the run stops when it reaches this charge.
_maxChargeUsd.title: Max charge (USD)

_maxItems.description: How many dataset items to return to the model (1-1000, default 50). Truncates the response only; it does not change what the Actor collects or charges for.
_maxItems.title: Max items returned

channels.description: Public channels to read. Any of these forms works: durov, @durov, t.me/durov, t.me/s/durov, https://t.me/durov, or a single post URL such as https://t.me/durov/531 (that post only). Private groups, invite links (t.me/+hash) and channels with the web preview disabled are not readable and are reported in the run summary.
channels.title: Channels

includeChannelInfo.description: Push a channel row (title, description, subscriber count, media counters, avatar, verified flag) before that channel's posts. Costs one channel-info event per channel.
includeChannelInfo.title: Include one channel-info row per channel

maxConcurrency.description: How many channels are fetched at the same time (1 to 10). Pages inside a channel are always fetched one after another with a short delay.
maxConcurrency.title: Channels in parallel

maxPostsPerChannel.description: How many posts to collect from each channel, newest first (1 to 10000). Telegram serves 20 posts per page, so this also decides how many pages are fetched.
maxPostsPerChannel.title: Max posts per channel

maxTotalPosts.description: Hard cap on post rows across all channels in one run (1 to 1000000). The run stops cleanly when it is reached.
maxTotalPosts.title: Max posts per run (all channels)

onlyNew.description: Deliver only posts newer than the highest post id already delivered for that channel. The cursor is kept in the named key-value store below, so scheduled runs return just the new posts.
onlyNew.title: Only new posts (delta mode)

postedAfter.description: ISO date or date-time. Posts older than this are skipped, and paging stops as soon as a page reaches older posts. Example: 2026-08-01 or 2026-08-01T09:00:00Z.
postedAfter.title: Only posts after this date (optional)

postedBefore.description: ISO date or date-time. Newer posts are skipped (paging still starts from the newest page). Example: 2026-10-01.
postedBefore.title: Only posts before this date (optional)

proxyConfiguration.description: Direct requests are the default: t.me answered 10 of 10 parallel direct requests when this actor was built. Enable Apify proxy only if your runs are rate limited. A proxy failure fails the request; it never falls back to a direct request.
proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy configuration

searchQuery.description: Only posts matching this text, using Telegram's own in-channel search (t.me/s/<channel>?q=...). Works with paging and with every other option. Leave empty to read the channel timeline.
searchQuery.title: Search inside the channel (optional)

stateStoreName.description: Name of the key-value store in your Apify account that keeps the per-channel post-id cursors. Leave the default unless you run several configurations of this actor and want separate cursors.
stateStoreName.title: State store name (delta mode)

name: telegram_channel
